finding.title: Cast an Ordinary Flag to Volatile to Force Reloads

reasons: target fireStreamingMovie__12TMarDirectorFUc improved from 74.16393 to 99.81967 but did not reach exact as claimed; runner records improved progress

finding.why: Seven flag-check/update pairs cast &unk4C to volatile u16*. The worker states this prevents common-subexpression elimination and reproduces repeated loads and scheduling. The field is an ordinary director flag, and no hardware or asynchronous-access contract was identified. This is a code-generation constraint substituted for an explanation of the original accessors or inline boundaries.
finding.score_attribution: The function improves 74.16393% to 99.81967%. The checkpoint also fixes selector 12 to take the default 0xF path; that jump-table-supported semantic correction is legitimate. Do not assign the entire gain to volatile or revert the selector fix with it.
finding.lint_candidate: Flag newly introduced volatile casts on ordinary game-object members unless an access contract justifies them.

occurrences.detail: Seven pairs in fireStreamingMovie, containing 14 volatile cast expressions. Compound assignment can perform both a read and a write; this is a source-expression count, not a machine-access count.

note.summary: No source change retained. Classified the residual as a broad instruction-shape mismatch involving switch block layout, stack-frame size, and operation scheduling. Tested moving every setNextStage call before the 0x100 flag update; this regressed the score from 74.16393% to 58.32787% and was reverted. Tested the existing checkUnk4CFlag/onUnk4CFlag helpers and explicit unk4C assignment syntax; both reproduced the baseline residual exactly and were ablated. The source-permuter probe could not locate the mangled function in the source, and instrumented MWCC diagnostics were unavailable.
